9139c5e47fc0.en: Including the awkward ones. If your question is not here, send it — we will answer it properly and then add it to this page.

b575114ce5f1.en: Cost, mostly, and it is a big gap — you will typically pay 35–55% less per piece than Portugal for the same construction, and our GSP+ origin means the duty into the EU is nil on most cotton garments where Turkey and Portugal carry none either but sit at a much higher base price. What you give up is proximity: a physical sample takes days longer to reach you, and a factory visit is a longer flight. If you need two-week turnarounds on repeats, Portugal wins. If you need a real price on a real quantity with a European company standing behind it, this is the better trade.

fc0135a41f7b.en: You own a clothing brand yourself. How do I know you will not copy my design?

80b50224269b.en: Fair question, and we would rather answer it than have you wonder. The group does own 7thstreet, a consumer brand — it sells in its home market only, and it has never carried a design made for a client. Our standard terms assign your designs, patterns, tech packs and blocks to you, and bar us from producing them for anyone, ourselves included. We will sign your NDA before you send anything, or send you ours. If that is not enough, ask us for a reference from a buyer whose designs we have held for two years.

1dbaebe17d90.en: What happens if you are late?

1e36c6e77126.en: So far it has not happened — thirteen orders, none late. That is a small sample and we will not pretend otherwise. What we commit to is this: your delivery date is confirmed in writing before you pay a deposit, you see the order move through the tracking system so a slip is visible weeks before it becomes a problem, and if we are the reason a date moves, we cover the air-freight difference to get you back on schedule. That last one is in the quote, not just on this page.

1f8257ba938a.en: How do you get fabric for a 10-piece order when mills sell in 300-metre minimums?

c76a5f548b8d.en: Three ways. We hold stock qualities in the fabrics we run most — jersey, fleece, piqué, 12 oz denim, 3×3 twill — so a capsule can come off fabric already on our shelf. We can piggyback your small run on a larger cut of the same quality when the timing lines up. And for anything we have to buy in specially, we will tell you the minimum before you commit rather than after. It is the honest reason a ten-piece run costs more per piece: you are carrying the set-up, not the fabric efficiency.

8d05fe4fbba4.en: Do you already make for a brand like mine?

3b0cb128af8c.en: Probably, and we will tell you plainly if there is a direct conflict. We currently ship denim and jersey for a UK brand, fleece programmes for a US buyer, twill workwear for an Italian label, denim jackets and cotton trousers for two more US accounts. We do not run exclusivity by category — there is not a factory in the world that could — but we do not share your tech packs, your fabric sources or your costings with anyone, and we will not put your pattern on someone else's order.

ebbfd6f7f40e.en: What about political unrest, port delays or an Eid shutdown?

14d61747389e.en: Our floor is inland and our fabric comes from domestic mills, so the disruptions that hit us are labour holidays rather than shipping lanes. Eid closes the floor twice a year for roughly a week each time, and those dates are published years ahead — we build them into your delivery date rather than discovering them later. Karachi port congestion is the real variable and it moves sailing dates by days, not months; we quote the sailing, not the arrival, and tell you which is which.

776f7ac78e4b.en: Yes, and you should if the order is big enough to justify the flight. We will host you, walk the floor and show you whatever you want to see. If you cannot travel, we do the reverse: a live video walk-through on your schedule, plus a physical sample box of garments off our own line so you can judge the quality with your hands rather than through a screen.

69e408fa08f1.en: What are your actual defect rates?

234bcb2f0b21.en: We inspect to AQL 2.5 on the major, which means an accepted lot has under 2.5% major defects by the standard sampling plan. Across the thirteen orders we have shipped no lot has been rejected on arrival and no customer has raised a quality claim. We would rather show you than tell you — ask for the inspection report from any order we have run and we will send it, including the minor non-conformances and how they were closed.

66faa7dbcb1c.en: Is that everything you can make?

449a31575c66.en: No — what is on the site is a sample of what we are asked for most, not the limit. The floor is a one-stop operation: fabric sourcing, design and pattern, cutting, sewing, printing, embroidery, labelling, packing and logistics, all under one roof. Between knit, woven, denim, workwear and leather we cover most of what a clothing brand or a company buying uniform actually needs — jeans in four- and five-pocket, chinos, cargos, shorts, towels in cotton terry, joggers, dungarees, coveralls, scrubs, rain suits, hi-vis, leather in cowhide, sheepskin, goat and buffalo. If the garment you want is not shown anywhere on this site, send us a photo or a sketch. The answer is usually yes, and when it is no we will tell you straight rather than take the order and struggle.

994063059cc8.en: Yes — 100% organic cotton across knitwear and woven, through the same mills we use for conventional qualities. It costs more per kilo and behaves differently in the wash, so we always sample it before you commit. Certificates are shared on request. We buy fabric per order and can source from more than one certified mill, so the paperwork is issued against your specific order rather than published as a generic certificate.

02722691b8d1.en: Why is the sample €50 when other factories send them free?

773a87fd97cf.en: Because a free sample is never free — it is priced into the bulk, and it tells you nothing about whether the factory takes you seriously. A sample costs us several hundred euros in pattern-making, a designer's time and a sample tailor on a machine that has stopped running bulk. We charge €50, we credit it in full against your first order, and in return you get a real garment in the fabric you chose, with your label, rather than a printed blank.

694a697cca8a.en: 50% to start development and buy fabric, 40% before shipping, 10% after you have inspected the delivery. No letter of credit, no bank guarantee, no cash against documents — you are paying a European company on an ordinary invoice. Companies and clubs buying kit can usually get 30-day invoice terms up to €5,000 after a credit check.

5ab34907c032.en: A factory that kept losing good brands to letters of credit and customs paperwork — and what we did about it.

5342ede0d1b6.en: The garment was never the problem.

b7c8842461d8.en: In 2011 a small workshop started cutting and sewing for other people's labels. Denim and jersey that ended up in the UK. Fleece programmes bound for the United States. Twill workwear for Italy. The garments were right. The dates were met. The customers came back and ordered more. By the standards of the trade, it worked.

ddccc0d80bc2.en: And still, over and over, we watched brands who wanted to buy from us walk away.

3fc45ce0b098.en: Not over price. Not over quality. They would see the samples, agree the costing, and then stop — somewhere between the quote and the first order, in a place that had nothing to do with clothing at all.

e4132013808a.en: Their bank wanted a letter of credit, which meant tying up cash for months on a first order they were not yet sure about. Someone had to be the importer of record for a container arriving from Asia, and it was not going to be a three-person brand in Amsterdam. They needed a customs broker they did not have and a freight forwarder they had never used. And at the end of all that, they were being asked to wire a five-figure deposit to a company they could not look up, in a country they had never visited, with no clear idea what they would do if the goods arrived wrong.

79015be57a2b.en: Underneath it sat the quiet one, the objection nobody says out loud: they could not order small. Every factory wanted a thousand pieces per colour. Which means a brand with a good idea and no warehouse has to bet an entire season on a guess — or never start at all.

17d078349428.en: We were solving the wrong problem, very well.

7b9c4b93fe66.en: It took us longer than it should have to see what that added up to. We had spent years trying to be a better factory — tighter stitching, faster sampling, sharper prices, a cleaner line. But not one of the things stopping those brands was happening on our floor. They were happening in a bank, in a customs office, and in a spreadsheet where somebody had typed “MOQ 1,000 pcs”.

d6d52905100d.en: The industry does have a standard answer to this, and we think it is a bad one. Put a middleman in: an agent, a trading house, a sourcing office — someone European-facing who takes the order, adds a margin, and passes it down a chain. It solves the paperwork by creating a worse problem. Now nobody is accountable. The agent blames the factory. The factory blames the fabric. The brand blames itself, and pays for all three.

c6ba7f1e5e05.en: So we moved the table, not the floor.

8c44c02879be.en: In September 2023 we did something a factory rarely does. We registered a company in the Netherlands — not a sales office, not a representative, not an agent taking a cut. The same owners, standing in front of the same floor. KVK 91485452, in the Dutch Handelsregister, where any buyer can look us up before sending a single euro.

5661816b35e4.en: Nothing about the making changed. Everything about the buying did. There is no letter of credit, because you are invoiced by a European company on terms. You are not the importer — we are, and the goods arrive at your door with the duty paid. And ten pieces became a real order, because the whole point was to let a brand find out whether an idea works before betting a season on it.

9b9b8f0c3d20.en: Since the European company started taking orders in March 2025 we have shipped 146,500 pieces and delivered over $1.2 million of orders into the UK, the United States and Italy. Eleven of the thirteen orders are repeat business. Buyers who come back typically triple the size of what they first ordered.

8b145e262846.en: That last number is the one we actually watch. Anyone can win a first order with a good price and a good sample. The second order is the only honest review a factory ever gets.

c81677d427f7.en: The floor is still the floor — the same one, running since 2011, now as Saee e Kamil in Pakistan, making for brands including Hype, HNO and UBST. What is new is that you no longer have to become an importer to buy from it.

47c28ee516a5.en: Take the risk off the buyer. No letter of credit, no importing, no customs broker, no wiring money into the unknown. One European invoice, in euros.
